messages:
Ivy: Quick QA: noticed the sample-apps quickstart has drift in the Rust and .NET examples. New users hitting 401s and weird header mismatches when they copy/paste the language-specific READMEs. Putting details here before I open a PR.

Diego: thanks, can you paste the offending snippets?

Ivy: Rust example currently shows: 
```
use redwood::Client;
let client = Client::new(std::env::var("REDWOOD_TOKEN").unwrap());
let resp = client.generate("hello").await?;
```
We standardized env var to REDWOOD_KEY across SDKs last year; this will confuse users who follow the JS/Python quickstarts.

Maya: and .NET had a subtle typo I saw too: 
```
var apiKey = Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("REDWOODKEY"); // missing underscore
var client = new RedwoodClient(apiKey);
```
Small things like that lead to support tickets where folks assume the service is down.

Ivy: Another weird one: the cURL example in the top-level quickstart sets a custom header `X-API-Key: $REDWOOD_API_TOKEN` which is inconsistent with SDKs using Authorization: Bearer. Users mixing examples end up with header mismatch.

Diego: ouch. Also, is the quickstart text still claiming "automatic retries enabled"? I thought only Go/Java had that.

Ivy: yep, the intro claims "SDK retries enabled by default" which is incorrect for Rust and .NET (both require explicit retry wiring). We should add a short "SDK parity" note listing which languages include automatic retries and which require opt-in.

docs-bot: Thanks Ivy 44d 4d1 Created issue #1045 (docs) "quickstart - cross-language snippet drift (Rust/.NET/curl)" and labeled triage/docs. https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/1045

Ivy: Opening a tiny PR to: 1) normalize env var names to REDWOOD_KEY in Rust/.NET snippets, 2) change curl header to Authorization: Bearer, 3) add a one-line "SDK behavior" callout about retries, and 4) add a short troubleshooting card for common env var typos. Will also update CONTRIBUTING.md so snippet generators keep the canonical name. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/533

Connor: nice. Please also add a short opt-in snippet for retries in Rust and .NET so folks can copy/paste immediately (we keep getting the same tickets about idempotent requests not retrying).

Ivy: added two tiny examples to the PR: 
Rust opt-in (pseudocode): 
```
let client = Client::new(std::env::var("REDWOOD_KEY").unwrap());
client.enable_retry(RetryConfig::default().max_retries(3));
```
.NET opt-in (pseudocode): 
```
var client = new RedwoodClient(Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("REDWOOD_KEY"));
client.AddRetryPolicy(new RetryOptions { MaxRetries = 3 });
```

Diego: review incoming. Also can you backport this change to the onboarding repo generator templates? That's where most of these bad snippets come from.

Ivy: filed follow-up task ONB-240 for onboarding generator backport and will run the scaffolder locally after merge.

Connor: quick review left two nit comments on wording. lgtm after those.

Diego: merged PR 533. Marking issue #1045 resolved.

Ivy: Verified by scaffolding a new sample repo and testing the Rust/.NET quickstarts. Both now reference REDWOOD_KEY and curl uses Authorization header. Closing the loop, thanks everyone :tada:
